entries.title: Positive local mass exponent
entries.statement: A positive Radon measure mu has finite positive local mass exponent a at x when mu(B_E(x,r))>0 for sufficiently small r and lim_{r->0} log(mu(B_E(x,r)))/log r=a with 0<a<infinity.

entries.title: Logarithmic disk potentials preserve positive local mass exponents
entries.statement: Let mu be a positive Radon measure near x with finite positive local mass exponent a. The centered disk potential T(R)=(1/pi) integral_{B_E(x,R)} log(R/|x-y|) mu(dy) is finite and positive for sufficiently small R, and lim_{R->0} log(T(R))/log R=a. This is a Euclidean potential exponent, not a metric Hausdorff dimension or sample-path exit-time theorem.
entries.proof_text: The positive exponent excludes an atom at x. Tonelli gives pi*T(R)=integral_0^R mu(B_E(x,s)) ds/s. For every 0<eta<a, the mass is eventually between s^(a+eta) and s^(a-eta). Integration bounds pi*T(R) between R^(a+eta)/(a+eta) and R^(a-eta)/(a-eta). Taking log exponents and then eta->0 proves the claim.

entries.title: Conditional clock-to-distance exponent cancellation
entries.statement: Let gamma,xi>0 and Q>alpha. If mu has local Euclidean mass exponent gamma*(Q-alpha) and a positive distance observable delta(r) has log(delta(r))/log r -> xi*(Q-alpha), then its logarithmic disk potential T(r) satisfies log(T(r))/log(delta(r)) -> gamma/xi. The metric scaling law is an assumption: putting xi=gamma/d_gamma does not calculate d_gamma.
entries.proof_text: The logarithmic-potential lemma gives the numerator exponent gamma*(Q-alpha). Divide it by the assumed positive distance exponent xi*(Q-alpha); the common factor cancels. No independence or product of conditional bounds is used.
assumptions: positive Radon mu with mass exponent gamma*(Q-alpha)
positive delta with the stated scale exponent

entries.title: Subcritical disk GMC logarithmic potential exponent
entries.statement: Fix 0<gamma<2. For the zero-boundary GFF on the unit disk, with covariance singularity log(1/|x-y|), let mu_gamma be the GMC of Lebesgue measure defined by the weak limit of 2^(-n*gamma^2/2) exp(gamma*h_{2^(-n)}(y))dy. Almost surely, for mu_gamma-almost every interior x, the centered logarithmic disk potential T_x(r) has log exponent 2-gamma^2/2. A strictly positive continuous local weight multiplying mu_gamma preserves this conclusion. This is a derived Euclidean-potential corollary, not an exact metric dimension formula.
entries.proof_text: Falconer--Jin, arXiv:1601.00556v4 Corollary 2.3, applies because the disk satisfies (A0), Lebesgue measure has exact dimension 2, and gamma^2/2<2. It gives positive mass exponent 2-gamma^2/2. Apply the logarithmic-potential lemma. A positive continuous weight is locally bounded above and below; hence weighted mass and potentials are bounded by constant multiples and the null sets agree. See LEMMA_GMC_COROLLARY.md for source and scope.
assumptions: dyadic circle-average GMC normalization as stated

entries.statement: DRAFT OPEN GAP, no solution of P0297: the Euclidean local GMC exponent 2-gamma^2/2 fixes a logarithmic-potential clock exponent but does not numerically fix the exponent converting Euclidean disks to actual strong-LQG metric radii. entries.title: Proposed correction of the D0049 LQG dimension identity
entries.statement: SOURCE CORRECTION PROPOSED, unlanded: D0049-A001 in probability_1000_intake_D_20260908/attempts.jsonl writes d_gamma=2Q/xi in two fields. For the standard metric parameter xi=gamma/d_gamma, the correct relation is d_gamma=gamma/xi. At the established Brownian-map value gamma=4/sqrt(6), xi=1/sqrt(6), Q=5/sqrt(6), the wrong expression is 10 and the correct one is 4. This refutes that recorded identity, not the general dimension problem. Primary support: Gwynne--Miller arXiv:1905.00383v3, equation (1.5) and Problem 7.1. Independent source-row review is pending.
assumptions: two-field source patch has not been applied

Apply the potential exponent conclusion with a=gamma*(Q-alpha), then divide by the separately assumed distance exponent.
Subcritical disk GMC supplies the positive local exponent a=2-gamma^2/2 required by the deterministic lemma.
The conditional ratio gamma/xi shows precisely why inserting the unknown xi does not evaluate a metric dimension.
The known Euclidean potential exponent is the proved part of the route; the actual metric exponent remains missing.
The route addresses the stored problem of computing the almost-sure Hausdorff dimension of the actual gamma-LQG metric.
